claims.claim: Events, interpretations, feelings and actions are analytically distinct even though they can influence each other rapidly. An event is observable information; interpretation is the meaning assigned; a feeling is subjective experience; an action is behaviour. Appraisals can vary between people and across contexts. This educational distinction is not a claim that every emotion is preceded by a conscious thought. Recognising alternative interpretations can prevent premature certainty; it must never be used to dismiss credible danger.
